correctness.rationale: Rebuilt proof: \(\(N_T\)(f)\ge\|f\|_1\) via weighted RMS-AM and \(\(N_T\)(f)\le S\|f\|_1\) via \(\ell^2\le\ell^1\) and invariance. On \(P_m\) group positive weights by congruence classes; Borel cross-section has positive measure and spike attains \(S_m\). On sets of arbitrarily long orbits construct positive-measure cylinder with L+1 pairwise disjoint iterates using a countable basis, yielding arbitrarily close ratios \(S\); bounded-period decomposition gives maximum of \(S_m\). Strict positivity ensures \(\(S_m\)<S\) and forces any hypothetical full-\(S\) maximizing support to have infinitely many positive-measure pairwise-disjoint translates, impossible. Pairwise \(\ell^1\)-to-\(\ell^2\) defect inequalities prove exactly the quantified near-extremizer iff, controlling infinite tails by \(\sum_k\sqrt{a_k}\). All quantifiers, complex moduli, null sets and infinite sums checked; finite numerical examples are supplementary only.

value.rationale: The focal 2026 paper explicitly makes the new smooth Daugavet norm quantitative only through a general upper bound. Determining its optimal isomorphic distortion is a natural functional-analytic quantity. The theorem shows a non-obvious exact orbit-period cutoff, with explicit residue-class weight aggregation, a sharp attainment/nonattainment phase transition, and an iff profile of all near-extremizers; all hold simultaneously for general invertible standard Borel probability actions rather than only one engineered finite sample. This is a motivated natural complete classification, not a textbook restatement of Jensen or a table lookup.
